history.description: John McCawley settled near the Little Wabash River, establishing 'McCawley's Tavern,' which became an early stagecoach stop and trading center for the region.
Following the placement of the Ohio & Mississippi (O&M) Railroad, J.D. Perkey officially established Clay City on the north side of the tracks.
The neighboring village of Maysville, the former county seat of Clay County, was formally incorporated into the Village of Clay City.
The discovery of oil in the area significantly shifted the local economy, leading to the development of various oil-related industries that continue to operate today.
As of the 2020 Census, Clay City remains a close-knit community with a population of 847, known for its deep agricultural roots and history as a transportation gateway.
